text:
Maya: Quick reminder — we cut release notes for v0.9.3 today at 17:00 PT. Please add entries (one-liners) to the release-notes.md PR before cutoff. Follow the tiny template below so the parser doesn't choke. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Jon: Do we still want the full Keep-A-Changelog headings or just the short bullets?

Maya: Short bullets. The release parser expects: Summary / Why / Impact / Migration (if any). Example in the template. No long essays, just 1-2 lines each.

Priya: Noted — updating my PR now. Will tag the feature flagging note as Migration.

release-bot: Automated check: release-notes.md parse failed for PR #4821 (bad quote char on line 12). See: https://ci.example.com/job/4821/logs

Alex: Ugh curly quotes again. Quick fix: replace smart quotes with straight ones, or run `scripts/release/fix-notes.sh` from the repo root.

Jon: Pinged @Priya on the PR with suggested edit (also removed an extra header).

Priya: Fixed & pushed. CI Bot — could you re-run the parser check?

CI Bot: Re-run requested by Priya — job queued.

Maya: Two tiny housekeeping items: 1) if your change affects API surface, add Impact and Migration. 2) Prefix entries with the component tag in square brackets, e.g. [runtime], [console], [docs]. That helps grouping in the release notes.

Jon: If anyone's late, we can pick up noncritical entries after cut if they are low risk, but they won't show in the official bullet list.

Alex: Branch coordination note — please avoid rebasing the release-notes branch after 16:30 PT. It causes the deploy script to misread the merged commit range.

Priya: A11y doc update is in PR #4830 and follows the template. cc @Maya

Maya: Thanks — I'll do a final sweep at 17:10 PT and squash minor duplicates. If you want an entry promoted to the headline section, DM me with justification. :+1:

release-bot: Reminder scheduled — release notes cutoff for v0.9.3 at 17:00 PT (in 1h).

Jon: Got it. I'll add my tiny typo fix in 10m.

CI Bot: Parser check passed for PR #4821 and #4830. All green.

Maya: Awesome. Thanks team — ship it.
